maya: Quick heads-up — ran a sensitivity scan across quant schemes (FP8, INT8, GPTQ, AWQ) for rwlm-3b on our structured tool-calling eval set. Short summary then logs.

sanjay: Nice. Which eval and seed? can you paste the run command?

maya: dataset: /evals/struct-toolargs/v2 (5k prompts). seed=42. commit=3fa7b2d
Command:
```
PYTHONPATH=./tools python -m evals.run --model rwlm-3b --quant awq,int8,gptq,fp8 --eval struct-toolargs --batch 8 --seed 42
```
Summary (token-level and schema pass rate):
- fp16 baseline: schema_pass=99.3%, toolarg_f1=0.964
- fp8: schema_pass=98.7% (-0.6pp), toolarg_f1=0.961 (-0.003)
- awq: schema_pass=95.6% (-3.7pp), toolarg_f1=0.949 (-0.015)
- gptq: schema_pass=92.9% (-6.4pp), toolarg_f1=0.941 (-0.023)
- int8 (per-layer): schema_pass=91.2% (-8.1pp), toolarg_f1=0.923 (-0.041)
Observed: fp8 mostly fine; AWQ/GPTQ/INT8 show structured-output drift and more truncation in toolargs.

eli: interesting. Did you test streaming vs batch? kv-cache/prefix handling can amplify errors.

maya: yes. streaming (token-by-token) shows ~1.2x higher schema failures for AWQ/GPTQ vs batch. suspected cause: quantized attention kernels + early-stopping heuristics. example bad output (AWQ):
```
{"action": "search", "args": {"q": "open-source quantizatio...
```
truncated and missing closing brace, then continued text not valid JSON.

ciara: can you paste a concrete toolarg mismatch case? we need to triage false positives vs semantic drift.

maya: sample prompt + two outputs (fp16 vs awq):
Prompt: "Find docs for CUDA fused kernels and return toolcall {tool:search, args:{q:\"cuda fused kernels\"}}"
fp16 -> `{"tool": "search", "args": { "q": "cuda fused kernels", "limit": 5 } }`
awq -> `{"tool": "search", "args": { "q": "cuda fused kernels", "limit": 5 }`  <-- missing `}`
Also saw arg-type corruption: `\"limit\": \"5\"` (string) under some int8 runs.

ben: two quick mitigation ideas:
1) add an output schema validator that attempts to auto-repair simple truncation (append `}`) as a last-resort fallback, log and count.
2) layerwise quantize-only feedforward/attn separately and rerun to see hotspots.

devon: i'll kick off per-layer ablations on a 8xA100 job. what CI config did you use? batch size/shard details?

maya: batch=8, seq_len=1024, prefetched_kvcache disabled. eval flag `--enforce_struct_schema=False` for raw samples. run name: quant-sensitivity-1976-R1
commit: 3fa7b2d

ops-bot: job quant-sensitivity-1976-R1 completed on gpu-cluster-5, artifacts: s3://redwood-inference/ci/quant-sensitivity/1976012345

sanjay: next steps:
- devon: per-layer ablation + report by layer index
- ciara: add deterministic schema-validator hook in eval harness and count auto-repairs
- ben: prototype auto-repair heuristics (closing braces, convert numeric strings)
- maya: collect sample diffs and open a regression issue with top 20 failing prompts

maya: added issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-4721 (notes + top 20 samples)

eli: also try fp8 mixed with 4-bit AWQ for FFN layers (hybrid quant) — anecdote: it keeps attention numeric stability but gains perf.

ciara: will add a unit test that runs 200 prompts through quantized model in CI (cheap smoke) and fails on >1% schema regressions.

devon: starting jobs now. ETA ~2.5h. ping me if you want shared Jupyter to inspect.

maya: thanks all. I'll aggregate logs into the analysis doc and drop a short PR to the evals harness with schema stats.
